messages:
alice: Quick heads-up — we're planning a short maintenance push to the runtime tomorrow 02:00 UTC. Need a status-page blurb + customer email draft. Keeping it to 15m change window.

emily: tagging this for comms. want a one-liner for statuspage + a slightly longer email. i can draft both.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: runtime-service v3.2.1 -> prod (canary=2, group=standard). CI: green.

carla: hold on — can we pin Dedicated customers to v3.1.x during the rollout? last time we saw perf regressions on quantized models in 3.2.1.

ben: +1 to pinning. we should add an automatic fallback policy for affected tenants too. idea: route Dedicated -> pinned variant until they opt in.

nate: rollback criteria: 5% error rate increase OR 200ms p95 latency regression for 5m. if either triggers, manual rollback.

alice: agreed on criteria. carla — can eng add a quick flag to the routing layer to keep dedicated pinned for the next 24h?

carla: can do. patch ready, will deploy to routing-canary in 30m.

emily: draft statuspage blurb below — please review/shorten: 

```
Scheduled maintenance: We will perform a short update to the inference runtime on 2026-03-21 02:00 UTC. During the ~15-minute window, customers may experience brief request queuing leading to slightly elevated latency for some requests. No data loss is expected. If you are on Dedicated capacity and prefer to avoid automatic switching, contact support to pin your workload to the v3.1.x runtime during the window. We will post updates on this status page.

Impact: Possible short latency spikes; successful failover/fallback in case of regressions.

ETA: 15 minutes.
```

alice: looks good. shorten first sentence to "short update to the inference runtime" as above. also include link to KB for pinning (we'll insert later).

emily: email draft for customers (support -> ops review):

```
Subject: Planned maintenance — short runtime update (2026-03-21 02:00 UTC)

Hello —

We will perform a brief maintenance update to the Redwood inference runtime on 2026-03-21 at 02:00 UTC. The change window is expected to last ~15 minutes. During this time some API requests may see slightly increased latency or brief queuing. There is no expected data loss.

If you run mission-critical Dedicated capacity and want to avoid switching for this update, we can pin your environment to the previous runtime (v3.1.x) for 24 hours — reply to this message or open a support ticket and we will handle it.

What we will monitor:
- Request error rate (SLO threshold)
- P95 latency across routes

If we detect regressions we will roll back to the prior runtime and update the status page.

Thanks,
Redwood Support
```

ben: nit: add explicit UTC timezone in subject: "(02:00 UTC)" — emily already has that but good to repeat. also include a one-click contact link for enterprise customers.

nate: infra note: adding automatic KV cache warmup after deploy to reduce initial p95 blips. queued job will run for 10m post-deploy.

carla: routing flag deployed to routing-canary. starting a small canary deploy for runtime v3.2.1 to 5% traffic now. monitoring dashboards up.

deploy-bot: Canary progress: 5% -> 25% -> 50%. No errors detected.

alice: ok — proceed with statuspage update and send the scheduled email at T-6h. emily, please push to scheduled send.

emily: scheduled email queued for T-6h. statuspage entry ready, will publish 15m before window.

ben: one more precaution — add quicknote in status blurb: "If you see elevated latency >20 minutes after window, contact support". less noise but helps TTR.

emily: updated blurb with that line. final statuspage text below (copyable):

```
We are performing a short update to the Redwood inference runtime on 2026-03-21 02:00 UTC. The change window is expected to last ~15 minutes. During this time some API requests may experience brief queuing or elevated latency. If you see elevated latency that persists more than 20 minutes after the window, please contact support.

Dedicated customers who prefer to remain on the prior runtime can request a 24-hour pin by replying to your support contact.

We will monitor error rates and p95 latency; on regression we will roll back and post updates here.
```

alice: great. last check: are rollback playbooks ready? carla/nate?

nate: yes — playbook v2.4 has steps: trigger rollback (deploy-bot rollback command), re-route Dedicated to pinned variants, invalidate canary routing, warm caches.

carla: confirming engineers on pager. i'll stand by during the window.

alice: thanks all — closing thread. we will post any incident updates under this status page if needed. :white_check_mark:
